name: Should shower wall tile go all the way to the ceiling or stop lower?

mainEntity.name: Should shower wall tile go all the way to the ceiling or stop lower?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should choose based on shower enclosure height, ceiling clearance, and maintenance preferences. Stopping at standard showerhead height (roughly 72 to 78 inches) uses less material and reduces initial installation labor. Tiling all the way to the ceiling protects upper drywall from rising steam, eliminates peeling paint lines, and creates a seamless, modern look. Full-height tile is particularly beneficial in enclosed shower stalls with low ventilation, where trapped moisture regularly reaches the upper perimeter of the room.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tiling to the ceiling provides superior moisture protection against steam and looks seamless, while stopping around six to seven feet lowers tile and labor expenses.
